summary: The app is largely a local‑first mobile UI with encrypted on‑device storage, but the review uncovered several security gaps. Critical/high‑severity findings are the inclusion of vulnerable third‑party libraries (node‑forge, braces) and an insecure fallback storage implementation for the web build that stores the encryption key in clear‑text localStorage. A high‑severity risk also exists in the PDF export routine where user‑supplied text is embedded into HTML without escaping, opening the door to XSS/JavaScript‑enabled PDF attacks. Medium‑severity issues include missing input validation for numeric fields (amounts, mileage, tax rates) which could cause calculation errors or denial‑of‑service, and additional vulnerable dependencies (uuid, sprintf‑js). Low‑severity findings are the lack of a Content‑Security‑Policy for the web build and weak enforcement of backup passphrase requirements. All findings are currently unfixed.

findings.issue: uuid 7.0.3 contains an out‑of‑bounds write vulnerability (CVE‑2026‑41907). It is used for generating IDs for receipts/mileage entries.
findings.fix: Upgrade uuid to a safe release (>=13.0.1) which includes the fix, or switch to a different UUID generator.

findings.issue: The web fallback stores the 256‑bit encryption key and encrypted payloads in plain localStorage. This defeats the at‑rest encryption model for any web deployment and allows an attacker with access to the browser storage to decrypt all user data.
findings.fix: Either disable the web build for production or replace the fallback with a proper client‑side key derivation flow (e.g., ask the user for a passphrase and never persist the raw key). If a web version is required, store the key only in memory and protect it with a user‑provided secret.

findings.issue: PDF export builds raw HTML strings that interpolate user‑provided text (receipt notes, categories, purpose, etc.) without escaping. When rendered by expo‑print, malicious HTML/JavaScript can be embedded in the generated PDF, potentially leading to XSS or JavaScript execution in PDF viewers.
findings.fix: Sanitize or HTML‑escape all user‑supplied fields before embedding them in the HTML template. Consider using a safe templating library (e.g., DOMPurify) and avoid injecting raw strings into the HTML used for PDF generation.

findings.issue: Numeric fields such as amount are not validated for type, range, or NaN/Infinity values. Users could enter negative, extremely large, or non‑numeric values causing incorrect totals, crashes, or potential DoS.
findings.fix: Add client‑side validation: enforce amount > 0, parseable as a finite number, limit max digits. Show error helper text on invalid input.

findings.issue: Mileage miles and rate are stored without validation. Malformed values (negative miles, non‑numeric strings) can corrupt mileage deduction calculations.
findings.fix: Validate that miles and rate are non‑negative numbers within reasonable bounds before persisting.

findings.issue: The UI hints at a minimum 8‑character passphrase but enforcement is not guaranteed; weak passphrases make backup encryption vulnerable to brute‑force attacks.
findings.fix: Implement explicit validation: require a minimum length (e.g., ≥8 characters) and optionally strength checks (mix of character classes) before allowing backup creation.

deployment_actions.issue: node‑forge 1.4.0 (transitively pulled in) is vulnerable to CVE‑2026‑85393 – a signature forgery vulnerability in RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 verification. If any code in the app (or a future feature) uses RSA signatures, an attacker could forge them.
deployment_actions.fix: No fixed release exists yet: monitor the advisory and upgrade as soon as one ships; confirm whether the package is only a build-time dependency. Upgrade node‑forge to a version where the vulnerability is patched (>=1.5.0) or remove the dependency entirely if not needed.

deployment_actions.issue: braces 3.0.3 has CVE‑2026‑93687 – denial‑of‑service via stack overflow caused by deeply nested patterns. The library is not used directly but is present in the dependency tree.
deployment_actions.fix: No fixed release exists yet: monitor the advisory and upgrade as soon as one ships; confirm whether the package is only a build-time dependency. Upgrade braces to a non‑vulnerable version (>=3.0.4 or later) or prune it from the dependency tree if not required.

deployment_actions.issue: sprintf‑js 1.0.3 is vulnerable to CVE‑2026‑97058 – denial‑of‑service via unbounded precision specifiers. Although not used directly, it appears in the lockfile.
deployment_actions.fix: No fixed release exists yet: monitor the advisory and upgrade as soon as one ships; confirm whether the package is only a build-time dependency. Upgrade sprintf‑js to a fixed version (>=1.1.2) or replace its usage with a safer formatting library.

deployment_actions.issue: The web build does not set a Content‑Security‑Policy header. While the app is a client‑side SPA, lacking CSP can allow injected scripts (e.g., from the PDF export issue) to run if any DOM XSS is introduced later.
deployment_actions.fix: Configure the web server or static host to serve a CSP header that restricts script sources to self and disallows unsafe‑inline code. For Expo web builds, add a meta CSP tag in index.html as a fallback.
